relevance_note: Scoping review whose Tables 2-5 give per-patient treatment and response data for previously published PSTPIP1-associated inflammatory disease patients, with variants tied to some of them, e.g. "patient #12 had the G258A mutation (ID 6 in Supplementary Table S2)".
method_note: Scoping review (no new patients). In-scope people are the per-patient rows of Tables 2 (PAPA, 22 patients), 3 (PAMI, 8 patients), 4 (PASH, 7 patients) and 5 (PASS 3, PAPASH 1, PAC 1). PASH and PASS patients are included because the paper presents all these syndromes as PSTPIP1-associated inflammatory diseases (PAID); most of them have no PSTPIP1 variant reported. Labels: the first column 'ID article (IDPatient)/Cycles' (e.g. '19 (1)/1') restarts patient numbering in each table, so each person is labelled 'Table <n> #<IDPatient>' (the text's 'patient #8 (ID 16)' etc. use the same Table 2 numbers); source_reference_in_review copies the first-cycle cell, whose first number is the article ID in Supplementary Table S2 (not available). The supplementary tables S2-S11 are not in the file, so no ages, sexes (except PAPASH and PAC patients, named in text), countries or full variant lists per person. A Python script assembled the JSON from row cells I chose by reading; every span was checked verbatim by the script. Phenotypes: a 'Yes' (complete/partial response) in a PA, acne, PG or SH efficacy column was recorded as the feature observed; 'No' (legend: not response), '-' (legend: not applicable) and NA were not used for any feature, because 'No' is ambiguous (the text describes the third canakinumab-treated PAPA patient, whose acne cell is 'No', as improving 'without acne development'). Adverse-event cells (hepatitis B reactivation, MRSA infection, multiple infections, proteinuria, injection-site reactions, diverticulitis) were recorded as observed features; 'Multiple infections' was mapped to checklist 'recurrent infections'. Neutropenia for Table 3 #11 and #12 is inferred from 'did not resolve neutropenia in reported PAMI cases (IDs 32-34 ...)'. Variants: assigned to a person only when the text names the patient (#8 c.G904A, #12 G258A, #10 wild-type so no variant row) or when the cited article ID has exactly one patient in Table 2 (ID 1->#16, ID 3->#14, ID 4->#13 A230T; ID 8->#11, ID 13->#9 E250Q; ID 19->#1 listed under both A230T and E250Q, so both recorded). Patients from multi-patient articles (IDs 16, 17, 22, 29) and the 'unspecified mutations' patients get a PSTPIP1 row with 'not reported'. Heterozygous comes from 'All cases exhibited these mutations in heterozygosity' (PAPA group); not applied to the unspecified rows. All eight PAMI patients get E250K from the named-group sentence. The PASS patient ID 28 NLRP3 Q703K is left out (authors call it common in the general population, a possible risk factor). Contradictions in the paper: (1) PAMI has nine patients in Epidemiology but eight in Genotype, Efficacy and Table 3; (2) Efficacy text lists ID 32 for PAMI anakinra patients but Table 3 has no ID 32, and says corticosteroids were used with anakinra in ID 28 (a PASS article); (3) A230T is said to be in seven patients but the cited IDs cover ten Table 2 patients; (4) 'All cases exhibited these mutations in heterozygosity' versus patient #10 with a wild-type allele; (5) PASH ID 5 is described both as improving at week 24 and among three non-responders that discontinued; (6) Table 5 #2 has '-' in the PA column but the text reports partial relief from arthritis; (7) Abstract says 5,225 articles, Results 5,525.
